components.unit_test_strategy: Automated infrastructure compliance testing using InSpec and Ansible Molecule. Test suites verify that non-management subnets cannot reach diagnostic ports, discovery service accounts cannot run root write commands (e.g. rm, write to /etc), sudoers wrapper only permits designated read-only discovery binaries, and failed authentication attempts trigger syslog alert events.

low_level_design.exception_handling_strategy: Comprehensive multi-tier exception handling architecture: 1) Network & Transport Layer: MID Server long-polling failures trigger exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s up to 60s) with local queue preservation; socket timeouts (SSH 15s, WinRM 20s, SNMP 5s) mark unreachable IPs with 'Skipped - Port Unresponsive' without terminating schedule batches. 2) Credential & Authentication Layer: In-memory credential lookups that fail with HTTP 401/403 or Vault timeouts automatically retry against secondary clustered vault endpoints; permanent credential failures log a masked 'Authentication Failure' audit record and create an automated ServiceNow incident routed to the IAM Operations team. 3) ECC Queue Backpressure: When active ECC input depth exceeds 5,000 items, the DiscoveryScheduleCoordinator dynamically pauses pending schedule dispatches and scales ServiceNow background worker threads from 40 to 80. 4) IRE Data Integrity Layer: Ambiguous identification matches (multiple CIs matching identification criteria) trigger immediate creation of an IRE De-duplication Task, leaving existing CMDB records immutable to prevent data corruption. Reclassification mismatches (e.g. server re-imaged as router) are isolated in a staging table pending CCB manual approval. 5) ITAM Synchronization Discrepancies: Hardware model anomalies generate HAM reconciliation tasks; unnormalized software packages default to 'Unnormalized' status and trigger automated asynchronous submission to ServiceNow Content Service Machine Learning pipelines. 6) Cluster Node Outage: Automatic MID cluster heartbeat polling detects node failure within 60 seconds; uncompleted probes in 'processing' state are automatically reset to 'ready' in the ECC Queue and reassigned to surviving cluster nodes.

business_context.scope: The architecture encompasses ServiceNow ITOM Discovery engine configuration, Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) rules, clustered MID Server deployment on AWS EC2 and on-premises VMware hosts, external credential vault integrations (CyberArk and AWS Secrets Manager), and automated synchronization to HAM Pro (alm_hardware) and SAM Pro (cmdb_sam_sw_install, alm_license). Excludes end-user desktop/laptop discovery (handled via Agent Client Collector) and non-ITAM financial cost allocation pipelines.
business_drivers: Elimination of software license compliance audit penalties through continuous, automated SAM software inventory discovery and entitlement reconciliation.
Reduction of operational downtime and incident MTTR by establishing a single source of truth for all hybrid IT infrastructure and inter-CI dependencies.
Optimization of hardware asset lifecycle tracking (HAM) from procurement to disposal, preventing asset loss and optimizing physical/virtual host density.
Automated compliance enforcement with regulatory frameworks (PCI-DSS v4.0, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS Controls) regarding unauthorized assets and shadow IT.
business_context.purpose: Define the high-level system architecture for an enterprise-grade ServiceNow ITOM Discovery solution operating across hybrid AWS cloud and physical on-premises datacenter environments, providing accurate, automated data population for Configuration Management (CMDB), Hardware Asset Management (HAM Pro), and Software Asset Management (SAM Pro).
objectives: Establish robust, automated multi-tier autodiscovery across AWS VPCs and physical on-premises datacenter environments using clustered ServiceNow MID Servers.
Normalize, populate, and reconcile Configuration Items in the ServiceNow CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) aligned with CSDM 4.0 standards.
Automate hardware asset inventory data flows to populate HAM Pro lifecycle attributes, including serial numbers, chassis, model categories, and asset-to-CI relationships.
Automate software asset discovery to feed SAM Pro normalized software installations, edition detection, and cloud-optimized software license metrics.
Achieve discovery throughput exceeding 50,000 infrastructure CIs and 100,000 software installation records within scheduled 8-hour discovery windows.
constraints: Strict Network Boundary: Zero inbound firewall ports may be opened from the public internet or ServiceNow SaaS cloud into corporate AWS VPCs or on-premises datacenters; all communication must originate outbound from MID Servers over TLS 1.3 on TCP 443.

Credential Governance: Plaintext credentials are strictly prohibited on MID Server host file systems; dynamic credential resolution via CyberArk CCP and AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation is mandatory.
Resilient High Availability: Discovery infrastructure must reduce single points of failure, supporting automatic MID cluster failover within 60 seconds without dropping discovery execution state.

Heterogeneous Platform Support: Multi-tier autodiscovery must concurrently support AWS cloud environments (EC2, RDS, VPC, ECS/EKS) and diverse physical datacenter platforms (AIX, Solaris, Linux, Windows Server, SAN/NAS, SNMPv3 network appliances).
assumptions: Dedicated enterprise service accounts with read-only/least-privilege discovery permissions are provisioned across target systems and AWS IAM accounts.
AWS Direct Connect or resilient IPsec VPN provides reliable inter-datacenter and AWS-to-on-premises hybrid administrative connectivity.
ServiceNow instance is hosted on Washington DC or Xanadu release with active ITOM Discovery, HAM Pro, and SAM Pro licensing entitlements.
Internal firewall rules and AWS Security Groups permit probe traffic from MID Server IP addresses to target subnets on designated ports (SSH 22, WinRM 5985/5986, WMI 135/445, SNMP 161, HTTPS 443).

alternatives.comparison_to_recommended: Direct SaaS discovery requires inbound ingress ports through enterprise perimeter firewalls and AWS Security Groups into secure internal subnets, violating enterprise zero-trust perimeter network policy. In contrast, the recommended MID Server architecture strictly enforces zero inbound firewall openings via outbound-only TLS 1.3 long-polling through the ECC Queue.
weaknesses: Breaches strict enterprise security boundary mandate prohibiting inbound SaaS traffic

strengths: Maintains strict zero-inbound security boundary across AWS VPCs and physical on-premise subnets
Provides resilience through localized discovery execution and active-active cluster failover

high_level_design.solution_overview: The Hybrid ServiceNow CMDB Autodiscovery solution deploys a highly resilient, distributed, agent-based discovery architecture spanning Amazon Web Services (AWS) and on-premises physical datacenters. Clustered ServiceNow MID Servers operate within customer-controlled private networks, polling the ServiceNow SaaS ECC Queue over outbound-only TLS 1.3 connections to execute autodiscovery across compute, storage, networking, and software assets. Discovery data flows dynamically into the ServiceNow Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) to maintain a single source of truth within the CMDB under CSDM 4.0 standards. Reconciled technical data immediately populates and synchronizes Hardware Asset Management (HAM Pro) lifecycle records and Software Asset Management (SAM Pro) license normalization models. Enterprise credential vaults (CyberArk CCP and AWS Secrets Manager) provide just-in-time, least-privilege authentication without storing plaintext credentials on MID Server hosts.
high_level_design.data_flow_overview: Discovery operates via an asynchronous, outbound-only polling pattern: 1) ServiceNow ITOM scheduler initiates discovery and posts probe tasks into the ECC Queue. 2) Clustered MID Servers in AWS and on-premises poll the ECC Queue every 2-5 seconds over outbound HTTPS (TCP 443). 3) Upon retrieving a probe job, the MID Server queries the local credential broker (AWS Secrets Manager in AWS; CyberArk CCP on-premises) over TLS 1.3 to obtain temporary target credentials. 4) The MID Server executes the probe against target endpoints (AWS Cloud APIs, SSH, WinRM, WMI, or SNMPv3). 5) Probe responses containing raw system configurations and software manifests are captured in memory. 6) The MID Server encrypts and delivers the payload back to the ServiceNow ECC Queue as an 'input' record. 7) ServiceNow ITOM sensors process the payload and submit it to the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE). 8) IRE applies identification rules to match existing CIs or create new records in cmdb_ci_* tables, preventing duplicates. 9) IRE triggers asset synchronization: hardware specifications (serial, MAC, chassis) update alm_hardware in HAM Pro, while installed software packages populate cmdb_sam_sw_install. 10) SAM Pro executes normalization and reconciles licenses against alm_license entitlements.

availability_and_resilience.disaster_recovery_plan: Enterprise disaster recovery spans all architectural tiers: 1) ServiceNow SaaS Platform (ITOM Discovery, IRE, HAM/SAM Asset Lifecycle Engines) utilizes multi-datacenter Advanced High Availability (AHA) automated geographic failover with near-zero data loss. 2) Enterprise Credential Vault Gateway leverages cross-region CyberArk Vault disaster recovery replication and AWS Secrets Manager cross-region secret replication. 3) Clustered MID Server instances absorb workloads during AZ or physical rack failure via active-active cluster pools; in total datacenter or region loss, MID Server clusters can be fully redeployed into alternate VPC/DC within 2 hours using automated Terraform IaC pipelines.
availability_and_resilience.backup_strategy: ServiceNow SaaS automated multi-region daily full database snapshots and continuous WAL journaling; MID Server configuration and custom discovery patterns stored in Git and provisioned via automated Terraform / Ansible templates.
availability_and_resilience.availability_target: 99.9% uptime for the hybrid discovery pipeline
availability_and_resilience.redundancy_strategy: Multi-tier redundancy, active-active clustering, and automated failover across all architectural tiers: 1) ServiceNow ITOM Discovery Engine & IRE: Deployed on a redundant, multi-node ServiceNow Advanced High Availability (AHA) clustered architecture within paired enterprise datacenters. Active-active application nodes share ECC Queue processing load, and the Percona MariaDB database cluster provides automated synchronous replication and sub-60-second database failover, mitigating single points of failure. 2) ServiceNow Asset Lifecycle Engine (HAM Pro & SAM Pro): Runs across the clustered ServiceNow multi-node application server pool with distributed asynchronous background worker threads (GlideScriptedHierarchicalWorker). Reconciliation and normalization jobs fail over transparently to surviving nodes, providing high availability without a single point of failure. 3) Enterprise Credential Vault Gateway: High-availability multi-instance clustered deployment across both environments: on-premises CyberArk Central Credential Provider (CCP) operates as an active-active clustered pool of stateless IIS web servers behind redundant F5 BIG-IP load balancers with automated health checks and sub-second VIP failover; AWS Secrets Manager is natively distributed across multiple AWS Availability Zones with multi-AZ VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink), delivering automated failover and 99.99% availability SLA. 4) Clustered MID Server Arrays: Clustered MID Server arrays with N+1 redundancy across independent AWS Availability Zones (us-east-1a, us-east-1b) and isolated physical on-premise hypervisor hosts and racks, providing resilience through active-active load distribution and automated failover within 60 seconds without dropping discovery execution state.

scalability_and_performance.scaling_strategy: Explicit elastic scaling strategies and technologies across all structural bottleneck and processing tiers: 1) ServiceNow ITOM Discovery Engine & IRE: Elastic scaling leveraging ServiceNow Advanced High Availability (AHA) dynamic application node pooling and an elastic ECC Queue worker pool. Worker threads automatically scale from 40 to 80+ concurrent threads based on queue depth thresholds (glide.ecc_queue.max_active_processing_jobs), while MariaDB read replicas elastically offload read-intensive CI identification queries to prevent database lock contention. 2) Enterprise Credential Vault Gateway: Horizontally elastic architecture. On-premises CyberArk Central Credential Provider (CCP) deploys an elastic pool of stateless REST API web service instances auto-balanced by F5 BIG-IP with connection pooling, handling surges in probe authentication requests without bottlenecking; in AWS, AWS Secrets Manager utilizes fully managed, elastic serverless VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) that scale automatically to support tens of thousands of API requests per second with built-in client-side jittered backoff. 3) Hybrid Target Infrastructure & Workloads: Elastic scaling across discovered environments. AWS workloads employ AWS Auto Scaling Groups (ASG) and Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) to dynamically adjust capacity; on-premises VMware vSphere clusters utilize VMware Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) to elastically balance CPU and memory allocations across ESXi hosts, preventing target host degradation during concurrent discovery probes. 4) MID Server Clusters: AWS Cloud MID Server cluster utilizes EC2 Auto Scaling Groups to dynamically scale instance count between 2 and 6 m6i.xlarge nodes based on ECC Queue output backlog; On-Premises Datacenter MID Server cluster supports rapid elastic expansion by deploying pre-hardened VM templates via Terraform within minutes to absorb burst scanning demands.
